mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A7 30 TFSI - 55 TFSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Audi A7 30 TFSI - 55 TFSI engine typically costs between £3,200 and £7,500 for supply only, depending on whether it is a 2.0L or 3.0L unit, with reconditioned units starting from £2,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of water pump failure in an Audi A7 30 TFSI - 55 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include coolant leaks under the vehicle or a distinct sweet smell from the engine bay. You may also experience an illuminated engine management light or the engine running hotter than normal.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Audi A7 30 TFSI - 55 TFSI (C7 generation)?

acceptedAnswer.text: For C7 models valued between £12,000 and £25,000, a full rebuild is highly financially viable for well-maintained examples. A reconditioned or rebuilt unit restores flagship reliability and comes with a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A7 30 TFSI - 55 TFSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit procedure for the 2.0L or 3.0L TFSI engine typically takes 2 to 3 working days at a specialist workshop.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CGWB and DZKA engines in the Audi A7 30 TFSI - 55 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CGWB is an earlier supercharged 3.0L V6 producing 290hp, while the DZKA is a modern turbocharged 3.0L V6 with a 48V mild-hybrid system producing 340hp. They feature entirely different forced induction architectures and are not directly interchangeable.
